conversation.content: When can I enroll in Medicare and select my coverage? And when can I make changes to my coverage after I've enrolled?

There are several key enrollment periods for Medicare:

Initial Enrollment Period (IEP):
- Begins 3 months before the month you turn 65
- Includes your birth month
- Ends 3 months after your birth month
- Total 7-month window

Annual Enrollment Period (AEP):
- October 15 - December 7 each year
- Can change Medicare Advantage or Part D plans
- Changes take effect January 1

Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment:
- January 1 - March 31 each year
- Can switch Medicare Advantage plans
- Can return to Original Medicare

Special Enrollment Periods (SEPs):
Available in special circumstances like:
- Moving
- Losing other coverage
- Your plan changing its contract with Medicare
- Qualifying for Extra Help

General Enrollment Period:
- January 1 - March 31 each year
- For those who missed Initial Enrollment
- Coverage starts July 1
- May include late enrollment penalties

It's important to enroll when first eligible to avoid penalties and gaps in coverage.
